title: Unified assured-PNT operational awareness and decision support (single pane for source health, composite confidence, jam/spoof triage, fallback recommendation) with a formation-level PNT interference picture feeding the C2/EW COP
problem: Shipboard navigation operators (and, later, vehicle crews and EW cells) must mentally fuse several fragmented displays of GPS/INS/alternate-source health to decide whether they are jammed, spoofed or broken and which fallback to take, with no composite confidence, no explainable recommendation, no audit trail, and no aggregation of local interference detections into a formation-level picture that the C2/EW common operating picture can use.

user.exact_role: Electronics Technician - Navigation (ETV/ETSW) and the navigation team (Quartermaster, Navigator, Officer of the Deck) on a surface combatant during transit of a contested strait; second user is the EW/spectrum or NAVWAR planner at battalion-through-theater echelons who needs a formation-level PNT interference picture.
user.echelon: individual_platform (initial); battalion_brigade to theater and joint (formation-level sub-scope)
organization_examples: U.S. Navy surface combatants equipped with GPNTS (PEO C4I / NAVWAR transition owner named in NP004)
Army MAPS/DAPS-equipped vehicle and dismounted units under PM PNT (later)
Joint Navigation Warfare Center (USSPACECOM) and Space Force NAVWAR cells

current_workflow: 1. ETV mans the navigation station only when there are navigation issues or during transit of a contested environment (NP004 Q&A, 2026-08).
2. Watches separate GPS receiver, INS, GPNTS and alternate-source indicators plus the ECDIS chart display - the Navy's own words: 'operators currently monitor several fragmented displays'.
3. Notices a divergence or alarm and manually infers the cause (hardware fault vs jamming vs spoofing) from raw indicators, C/N0 behavior and experience.
4. Consults TTPs/checklists and the OOD/Navigator; falls back to celestial, radar or dead-reckoning fixes as required by OPNAVINST 9420.1C.
5. Selects an alternate source or INS-only/degraded mode on the individual system HMI.
6. Records actions in the navigation workbook; reports interference to the EW cell, NAVCEN or fleet by voice/message - or not at all.
7. At formation level, the EW cell manually plots any reports; JNWC compiles assessments after the fact; civil channels (NAVCEN, MARAD, NATO Shipping Centre) run in parallel.
current_solution: Individual-system HMIs (GPNTS display, INS panel, GPS receiver front panels, alternate-source vendor dashboards), the ECDIS-N chart display, paper/PDF procedures, and backup fixes (celestial, radar, DR). Device-level interference detection exists inside MAPS/DAPS/GPNTS-class units (RECALL - not re-verified this session), and civil jamming maps/advisories exist outside DoD, but there is no vendor-neutral composite-confidence layer, no fallback recommender with rationale, and no automatic aggregation into the EW/C2 COP (INFERENCE from NP004 topic text and OPNAVINST 9420.1C waiver clause).
failure: Slow, error-prone anomaly triage under workload; wrong fallback selection; no explainable rationale or replay for after-action review; interference information not automatically passed to electronic-support efforts as OPNAVINST 9420.1C 5.a(11) intends (systems that cannot comply seek waivers); at formation level, latency of hours to days, manual re-entry and no link between interference geometry and the trustworthiness of tracks in the COP.

evidence.claim: Navy SBIR 26.5 CSO open topic DON26BX05-NP004 ('NAVWAR Open Topic for Unified Assured PNT Operational Awareness and Decision Support') states operators must 'interact with multiple interfaces and data sources' and that 'this fragmented environment increases cognitive workload, complicates training, and slows decision-making'; it seeks a 'single pane of glass' that ingests 3-8 simultaneous PNT sources at 1-10 Hz via ASPN/pntOS, derives a composite confidence, triages hardware fault vs jamming vs spoofing, recommends fallback with explainable rationale and auditable trace, and runs air-gapped in containers; GPNTS is the named transition owner. Pre-release 2026-08-05, open 2026-08-26, closed 2026-09-23. Read via a GitHub-mirrored capture (2026-09-07); primary page EGRESS_BLOCKED this session.
evidence.source_title: Navy CSO Open Topic DON26BX05-NP004 with Topic Q&A (mirror: DeepBlueDynamics research corpus)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: NP004 Q&A (2026-08-08 and 2026-08-20): 'Operators currently monitor several fragmented displays'; 'the baseline workflow is the current environment of monitoring multiple fragmented physical displays'; Q&A 2026-08-21: the capability 'should primarily accelerate anomaly triage (rapidly distinguishing between a hardware fault, jamming, or spoofing) and fallback execution'; Q&A 2026-08-26 success metrics are 'speed to decision during an anomaly, threat comprehension accuracy, decision accuracy (e.g., correct fallback selection)'.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO technology assessment: alternative PNT is 'not prioritized', 'there is no central program office', requirements are unclear, 'determination of assurance is an active research area' across source-level and consensus approaches, and 'because of this proprietary nature, there are few opportunities to integrate alternative PNT technologies'; DoD funded the open-architecture (ASPN/pntOS) fix at $17M FY2020-2024 against $783M of PNT S&T and an expert warned it may 'peter out'.

If a new PNT system is unable to comply... submit a waiver' - a standing requirement that the 2026 NP004 topic shows is still unmet at the integrated-display level.

Public evidence insufficient beyond policy statements.

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Until 2026 the data was locked inside proprietary receivers and program-specific ICDs ('few opportunities to integrate', GAO-21-320SP), so the only firms that could see multi-source health were the receiver/fusion primes (Collins, BAE, L3Harris) and the government's own pntOS engineering house (IS4S), none of whom are rewarded for a vendor-neutral layer. The buyer sat between navigation (OPNAV N2N6/GPNTS), EW (NAVWAR/EW cells) and C2 (Overmatch/NGC2) owners with nobody responsible ('everyone's need, nobody's business'), and alt-PNT S&T is documented proto-purgatory ($783M S&T vs $17M integration). PNT startups chased the deep-value hardware layers (quantum sensors, LEO-PNT, timing) where venture money and DIU TQS attention were; the awareness/decision layer looked like a dashboard feature, not a company. Only in 2026 did NAVWAR publish a software-only topic, accept synthetic ASPN/pntOS data, and did the schemas go public. For the formation-level sub-scope, aggregated threat pictures drift toward CUI/classified EW products owned by JNWC and EW primes.
technical_wedge: A source-agnostic 'PNT integrity graph': ingest ASPN 2023 measurement/estimate/integrity messages (and, via adapters, NMEA/IEC 61162 and receiver telemetry such as C/N0, AGC, clock drift) from 3-8 sources; run deterministic consistency, ICD-compliance and consensus checks (DHS PNT Integrity Library style, INS-GNSS divergence, clock-holdover models, RAIM-like residuals) to produce a per-source health score and a composite confidence with attributed evidence; classify the anomaly (fault vs jam vs spoof) with an explainable rule/likelihood engine; recommend a fallback (alternate source, INS-only, degraded-ops workflow) with rationale; log an auditable, replayable event timeline; render on an S-52-conformant chart layer with IMO bridge-alert-management style alerts. Second stage: publish a compact interference-report message (integrity fields + geometry) over TAK/CoT or the Navy/Army data layers so an edge service can aggregate reports into denial-area polygons and per-track PNT-trust tags for the COP. The value is the assurance analytics, scenario library and replay - not the screen.

mvp.what: Containerized, air-gapped web application plus a synthetic strait-transit scenario generator (GNSS jamming/spoofing onset, INS drift, clock holdover, hardware fault) emitting ASPN 2023 messages; integrity engine; ECDIS-like HMI with source cards, composite confidence gauge, anomaly classification, recommended fallback with rationale, and an event timeline/replay; measured in a user study with former ETVs/QMs against the Navy's stated metrics (speed to decision, threat comprehension accuracy, correct fallback selection).
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for a strong engineer plus a navigation/integrity advisor: the open ASPN schemas, pntOS-C API, DHS PNT Integrity Library (BSD-3), GNSS-SDR, gnss-lib-py, public TEXBAT-type spoofing datasets and NOAA ENC cells are all available; a Docker/Kubernetes offline deployment and a 10-scenario library with recorded operator-study results is achievable within $50k-$150k.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: (1) Composite confidence and anomaly classification are correct and stable on held-out synthetic and public real-world jam/spoof recordings (false-alert rate, detection latency under 1 s at 1-10 Hz); (2) operators reach the correct fallback faster and with fewer errors than with fragmented displays; (3) every recommendation is explainable and replayable; (4) it can consume a pntOS/ASPN stream unchanged so a Phase II can swap in GPNTS ICDs; (5) it runs fully disconnected in a container that can pass Iron Bank/RAISE-style gates.

data_requirement.what: Phase I / MVP: synthetic ASPN/pntOS multi-source streams, public GPS ICDs (IS-GPS-200/705/800), public spoofing/jamming recordings (TEXBAT, Jammertest-type campaigns), NOAA ENC cells, USCG NAVCEN test schedules and MARAD advisories for realistic geography. Phase II / deployment: GPNTS ICDs and message types, the government ASPN message set, representative Navy data sets, JNWC standardized threat conditions, and receiver telemetry from fielded units; for the formation sub-scope, exercise ground truth (PNTAX/JNWC) and receiver integrity telemetry from MAPS/DAPS-class units.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: MVP data: yes, entirely public/synthetic (the Navy explicitly allows synthetic ASPN/pntOS data in Phase I). Government data: only post-award and CUI-handled (CMMC L2, DFARS 7012); the government ASPN message set requires citizenship/contractor verification at aspn.us, which may exclude a non-U.S.-person co-founder; real NAVWAR threat signatures are classified and reachable only through JNWC/PNTAX participation with cleared personnel.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes for the formation-level COP layer: Anduril/Palantir already hold the NGC2 data-layer baseline and Lattice/Maven fuse tracks, so an interference overlay is a feature for them; L3Harris/Collins/BAE control receiver telemetry and could expose it. For the shipboard operator layer, the GPNTS integrator or IS4S could add a screen, and the Navy could keep it government-developed. Incumbent-response risk is MEDIUM-HIGH for the operator layer and HIGH for the formation layer.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only if it owns the hard, unglamorous middle: a validated composite-assurance engine, a scenario/replay library with operator-study evidence, and conformance to open ASPN/pntOS and DHS CF behaviors that make it the reference implementation the Navy and allies can drop into any fusion engine. Primes have no incentive to build vendor-neutral assurance (it commoditizes their receivers) and NGC2 integrators lack PNT-integrity domain depth. If the team can only build a dashboard, reject: the screen will be absorbed.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The operator-awareness layer is unclassified CUI work: NP004 carries no ITAR banner, requires CMMC Level 2 (Self) and DFARS 7012 handling, and the Navy states no facility clearance is expected in Phase II (Q&A 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-01). Burden rises to high for anything touching M-code/PPS receivers (USML/COMSEC, RECALL), real NAVWAR threat data (classified per GAO), Link 16 time transfer, or the aggregated formation/theater threat picture (JNWC/EW products, likely classified). NAVWAR-compliance certification (DoDI 4650.08) applies to the host system, not the software alone, but any fleet PNT system must be certified as-designed and as-installed (OPNAVINST 9420.1C).
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: Three distinct constraints need counsel, none a definitive legal judgment here: (1) SBIR/STTR ownership and control by U.S. citizens/permanent residents (>50%) - affected by the German founder's residency timing and the Indonesian founder's status; (2) CUI/CMMC and the aspn.us government ASPN message-set citizenship/contractor gate may exclude a non-U.S.-person co-founder from Phase II data even though the work is unclassified; (3) ITAR technical-data access (deemed export) for any receiver/sensor path; plus FOCI mitigation if a facility clearance is ever needed for the formation-level scope.

dual_use_potential.explanation: The same composite-assurance and interference-triage engine maps onto DHS/CISA Resilient PNT Conformance Framework levels for critical-infrastructure timing, maritime operators facing global GNSS interference (MARAD 2026-008; NATO Shipping Centre reporting), and aviation/port authorities; commercial GNSS-monitoring vendors show a paying civil market exists. But civil buyers tolerate cloud connectivity and single-vendor receivers, so the air-gapped multi-source military variant is a distinct product; civil revenue is plausible but unproven (INFERENCE).

defensibility.explanation: Proprietary value accrues in the validated assurance algorithms and their operator-study evidence, the scenario/replay library (synthetic plus exercise-derived jam/spoof signatures), GPNTS/pntOS/ECDIS integrations, an accredited Iron Bank/RAISE container, and the GPNTS/N2N6 relationship. Open ASPN/pntOS standards cut both ways: they enable entry but also let a competitor plug in; defensibility therefore depends on being the trusted reference implementation, not on interface lock-in.

why_now: (1) First-ever dedicated solicitation for the software awareness layer with a program of record as transition owner (NP004, Aug-Sep 2026) and explicit acceptance of synthetic ASPN/pntOS data; (2) ASPN 2023 schemas (Jan 2026) and the pntOS C API (Apr 2026) became public, with ASPN stewardship reportedly moving to an industry consortium (Jul 2026, MEDIUM) - the proprietary-interface barrier GAO described in 2021 is falling; (3) GPS denial is now routine and global: a dozen-plus domestic DoD interference tests per month with radii to 295 NM and standing maritime advisories; (4) hardware assured-PNT (MAPS/DAPS Gen II) has reached production (RECALL), so multi-source data streams exist to be fused; (5) M-code remains late in all three segments (GAO 2024), so assurance software stays valuable regardless of hardware timelines.
killer_risk: Structural eligibility plus single-customer dependence: the only documented buyer path is a Navy SBIR topic that (a) closed on 2026-09-23 before the founders could bid, (b) requires >50% U.S.-person ownership and CUI/citizenship-gated data that a team with an Indonesian non-U.S.-person co-founder may not satisfy, and (c) is expected to draw multiple Phase I awards including IS4S and GPNTS-adjacent bidders. If the founders cannot clear SBIR eligibility, the remaining route is subcontracting or an OT with no published requirement, in a domain GAO calls 'nobody's business' with a documented pattern of demos that never transition. The formation-level sub-scope additionally drifts into classified EW territory and is absorbable by NGC2/Overmatch data-layer integrators.

allied_extension: More compelling, with caveats. Allied navies and coalition formations face the same fragmented-display problem and stronger real-world interference exposure (Baltic, Black Sea, Eastern Mediterranean and Red Sea GNSS interference; NATO Shipping Centre reporting channels cited in MARAD 2026-008), and the open ASPN/pntOS standards plus DHS CF behaviors give a releasable, unclassified basis for a coalition-shareable assurance layer. Project Overmatch's Five Eyes arrangement and the German founder's background suggest UK/Australian/German naval or Bundeswehr PNT-awareness pilots as a second market. Caveats: allied ships run different fusion engines and ECDIS suppliers, coalition releasability of aggregated interference pictures is unresolved (S06/S08 findings), and DoDI 4650.08 restricts transfer of equipment relying on foreign/commercial PNT sources - so allied revenue is plausible only for the unclassified operator layer, not the theater threat picture. HYPOTHESIS; not re-verified this session.
